note: Visual type-scale concept. Labels are proposed implementation sizes, not measured raster sizes. Body uses simplified companion lettering.
prompt:
Create a polished typography scale specimen for Math on Mars, using the attached Space Mission alphabet as the lettering reference. Portrait 1536x2048 target. Flat dark navy background, ivory primary text, cyan headings, golden numerical accents. No shading, glare, textures or 3D. Spacious highly legible editorial layout, one small plain label column on left and wide sample column on right, aligned vertically, generous outer margins. Heading top "SPACE MISSION" then small subtitle "TYPE SCALE / CONCEPT".
Use these exact labels and samples, each row visibly decreasing in size according to the nominal sizes:
"DISPLAY / 64 px" sample "MATH ON MARS"
"H1 / 48 px" sample "MISSION COMPLETE"
"H2 / 36 px" sample "Choose your upgrade"
"H3 / 28 px" sample "Twin-barrel blaster"
"H4 / 24 px" sample "Weapon stats"
"P1 / 18 px" sample across two lines "Explore the crater. Defeat the swarm." and "Solve each challenge to power up."
"P2 / 16 px" sample "Equip two ammo types before the next wave."
"BUTTON / 18 px" sample "START MISSION" in a simple cyan outlined button.
"CAPTION / 12 px" sample "Next wave in 00:15"
"HUD / 32 px" sample "HP 100   LEVEL 12"
"MATH / 40 px" sample "8 × 7 = 56"
Reference geometric broad rounded letter shapes closely for headings, button, HUD and math. For P1, P2, caption show an optically simplified companion treatment with thinner strokes, open counters and no stencil cuts or outlines, so small reading text stays readable. Make all labels plain understated sans serif. Preserve capitalization exactly. The size labels describe intended implementation scale, not literal image pixels. Footer small text "Visual concept — sizes to be tested in game". No illustrations or extra text.
